name: abnormal liver enzymes overview
title: Abnormal liver enzymes: the pattern first (hepatocellular ALT and AST, or cholestatic ALP and GGT), then how high and which enzyme leads, sorting into AST-led, ALT-led, severe, non-hepatic, cholestatic and ALP-alone causes, each with what to think of and the next step

root.title: Liver enzymes up: HEPATOCELLULAR or CHOLESTATIC pattern?
lines: enzymes mark DAMAGE or blocked bile flow; they are NOT tests of liver FUNCTION
is it FAILING? albumin ↓, bilirubin ↑, international normalized ratio (INR) ↑: INR is the fastest readout (short half-life)
then ask HOW HIGH, how FAST, WHERE (ethnicity, travel) and WHEN (age, drugs, comorbidities)

groups.title: HEPATOCELLULAR: alanine (ALT) and aspartate (AST) aminotransferase lead
lines: ALT is the liver-specific one; AST is also in red cells, muscle, brain, gut

groups.title: CHOLESTATIC: alkaline phosphatase (ALP) leads
lines: always read it WITH gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT)

tiers.title: MILD: up to 5-10× the upper limit of normal

head: h
AST > ALT
ratio > 2:1 is classic for ALCOHOL
cause: • alcoholic liver disease, cirrhosis of any cause
next: abstinence is step 1: CHRONIC LIVER FAILURE chart

head: h
ALT > AST
the longest list
cause: • viral, toxic or autoimmune hepatitis, celiac disease
next: WHERE and WHEN point the way
• from hepatitis B areas (SE Asia, Africa)

head: h
SEVERE: > 15× normal
acute injury
cause: • acute viral, toxic, ischemic or autoimmune hepatitis
next: INR > 1.5 + encephalopathy, < 26 weeks = ACUTE LIVER FAILURE

head: h
ALP + GGT ↑
hepatobiliary: GGT CONFIRMS it
cause: • primary sclerosing or biliary cholangitis, drugs, sepsis, parenteral nutrition
next: duct imaging after it: JAUNDICE chart

head: h
ALP alone
probably NOT the liver
cause: • pregnancy, normal childhood growth, bone disease
